# Enums

An enum item is written `Enum.<Name>.<Item>`. A property of an enum type
always holds one of the enum's items and is never nil; where 'not set' is a
valid state, the enum has an item for it.

## Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo

The frame in which a mover's vector is given.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Attachment0` | 0 | The frame of the first attachment, which follows its part as the part turns. |
| `Attachment1` | 1 | The frame of the second attachment. |
| `World` | 2 | The world's axes. |

## Enum.ActuatorType

What drives a hinge, a prismatic joint or a ball socket.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | Nothing drives the joint; it only constrains the parts. |
| `Motor` | 1 | The joint moves at a target speed. |
| `Servo` | 2 | The joint moves to a target position and holds it. |

## Enum.AlphaMode

How a `Material` uses the alpha channel of its base color. The three modes are those of glTF.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Opaque` | 0 | Alpha is ignored. This is the cheapest mode and suits most surfaces. |
| `Mask` | 1 | Each pixel is either drawn or not, by comparing its alpha with `AlphaCutoff`. Use it for leaves and fences. It needs no sorting and writes depth, like an opaque surface. |
| `Blend` | 2 | The surface is blended with what is behind it, by its alpha. Use it for glass and smoke. Blended surfaces are sorted and cost more to draw. |

## Enum.AnimationCullingMode

How often the meshes of an `AnimationPlayer` are posed.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Automatic` | 0 | As often as the meshes are visible. They are posed every tick up close, every second, fourth or eighth tick as they get smaller on screen, and not at all where neither the camera nor a shadow shows them. Clips keep advancing in every case, so a character is in the right pose as soon as it is seen. |
| `AlwaysAnimate` | 1 | Every tick, visible or not. Use it for a main character, or a character whose pose a script reads. |

## Enum.AntiAliasingMode

The method used to smooth edges.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Off` | 0 | No anti-aliasing. |
| `FXAA` | 1 | Fast approximate anti-aliasing: one pass over the finished picture that finds edges by contrast and softens them. It is the cheapest method and slightly blurs fine texture detail. |
| `SMAA` | 2 | Subpixel morphological anti-aliasing: three passes over the finished picture that find edges by their shape and blend them by coverage. It is sharper than FXAA and costs slightly more. |
| `TAA` | 3 | Temporal anti-aliasing: each frame is drawn with a subpixel offset and blended with the previous frames. It removes the shimmer of thin details in motion, such as fences, wires and distant grass, which a single frame cannot.<br><br>It applies to the main camera only. A `ViewportFrame`, a sub-world and a picture made only of sprites use SMAA instead. Pixel art among 3D surfaces is never offset or blended. |

## Enum.ApplyStrokeMode

What a `UIStroke` outlines.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Contextual` | 0 | The text of a text object, and the border of any other object. |
| `Border` | 1 | The border of the object, even for a text object. |

## Enum.AspectType

How a `UIAspectRatioConstraint` sizes its object.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FitWithinMaxSize` | 0 | The object becomes the largest rectangle of the ratio that fits inside its own size. |
| `ScaleWithParentSize` | 1 | The dominant axis takes the parent's full extent, and the other axis follows from the ratio, even if it exceeds the parent. |

## Enum.AssetFetchStatus

The outcome of one item of `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Success` | 0 | Every asset the item uses is loaded. |
| `Failure` | 1 | An asset the item uses could not be found or read. |

## Enum.AutomaticSize

The axes on which a `UIObject` sizes itself to fit its contents, ignoring `Size` on those axes. Use it for text and lists, so that a label is never smaller than its text.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | Neither axis: `Size` is used as set. |
| `X` | 1 | The width fits the contents. |
| `Y` | 2 | The height fits the contents. |
| `XY` | 3 | Both the width and the height fit the contents. |

## Enum.BlockOpacity

How much of what is behind a block of `VoxelService` shows through it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Opaque` | 0 | Nothing shows through. A face against the block is hidden, and the block darkens the corners it touches. |
| `Cutout` | 1 | The block has holes where its image is transparent, as for leaves, a fence or a grate. Each pixel is either drawn or not. The faces between two cutout blocks are drawn, which makes foliage look full. |
| `Translucent` | 2 | The block is blended with what is behind it, as for glass, water or ice. No face is drawn between two blocks of the same type, so a lake has a single surface. |

## Enum.BorderStrokePosition

Where a border `UIStroke` lies relative to the edge of its object.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Outer` | 0 | Entirely outside the object. |
| `Center` | 1 | Centered on the edge: half outside and half inside. |
| `Inner` | 2 | Entirely inside the object. |

## Enum.CameraProjection

How a `Camera` projects the world onto the screen.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Perspective` | 0 | Distant objects look smaller, according to `FieldOfView`. Use it for 3D. |
| `Orthographic` | 1 | Objects keep the same size at any distance. The view extends `OrthographicSize` meters from its center to its top edge. Use it for 2D: the camera looks along its -Z axis, so a 2D world on the XY plane faces it. |

## Enum.CharacterState

What a `CharacterBody` is doing.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Grounded` | 0 | Standing on ground it can walk on. |
| `Airborne` | 1 | Not supported by walkable ground: jumping, falling, or on ground too steep to walk on. |
| `Swimming` | 2 | Its middle is below the surface of a `Water` or inside a fluid block. Gravity does not affect it, and it moves on all three axes. |
| `Flying` | 3 | `CharacterBody.Flying` is on. |

## Enum.CollisionFidelity

How closely the collision shape of a `MeshPart` follows its mesh. A closer shape costs more to simulate.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Default` | 0 | The engine chooses the shape. It currently uses `Hull`. |
| `Hull` | 1 | One convex hull around the whole mesh. |
| `Box` | 2 | The bounding box of the mesh. This is the cheapest shape and the least accurate. |
| `Precise` | 3 | The triangles of the mesh. It is not implemented yet: a part set to `Precise` collides as `Hull`. |

## Enum.DecalBlendMode

How a `Decal` is combined with the surface it lands on.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Multiply` | 0 | The image multiplies the surface: it darkens and tints and cannot brighten. Use it for a stain, a shadow or a scorch mark. |
| `Alpha` | 1 | The image is laid over the surface by its alpha, and lit like the surface. Use it for a painted sign or a marking that must be readable on any ground. |
| `Additive` | 2 | The image's light is added to the surface, unlit. Use it for a glow, an aura or a magic circle. |

## Enum.DominantAxis

The axis a `UIAspectRatioConstraint` takes from its parent when it scales with the parent's size.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Width` | 0 | The object is as wide as the parent, and its height follows from the ratio. |
| `Height` | 1 | The object is as tall as the parent, and its width follows from the ratio. |

## Enum.Dormancy

Whether a part may sleep where no player is near, set by `BasePart.Dormancy`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Auto` | 0 | It sleeps on a dedicated server when no player's focus is within the game's `dormant_radius`: a `CharacterBody` does not walk, and what it was asked waits. |
| `Never` | 1 | It stays awake wherever it is: a train, a projectile, a boss that roams. |

## Enum.EasingDirection

Which end of a tween the easing applies to.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `In` | 0 | Eased at the start and abrupt at the end. |
| `Out` | 1 | Abrupt at the start and eased at the end. This is the usual choice. |
| `InOut` | 2 | Eased at both ends: the `In` curve over the first half, mirrored over the second. |

## Enum.EasingStyle

The shape of the curve a tween follows. The styles are the standard easing functions used by animation tools.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | 0 | No easing: constant speed. The easing direction has no effect. |
| `Sine` | 1 | A gentle curve based on a sine wave. |
| `Quad` | 2 | A curve based on the square of the progress. A mild acceleration. |
| `Cubic` | 3 | A curve based on the cube of the progress. Stronger than `Quad`. |
| `Quart` | 4 | A curve based on the fourth power of the progress. Stronger than `Cubic`. |
| `Quint` | 5 | A curve based on the fifth power of the progress. Stronger than `Quart`. |
| `Exponential` | 6 | An exponential curve: very slow at one end and very fast at the other. |
| `Circular` | 7 | A curve shaped like a quarter of a circle. |
| `Back` | 8 | Overshoots the end and comes back. The value goes outside the range between start and goal, so the tweened property must accept that. |
| `Bounce` | 9 | Settles by bouncing, like a dropped object. |
| `Elastic` | 10 | Oscillates past the end before settling, like a spring. Like `Back`, the value goes outside the range between start and goal. |

## Enum.ElasticBehavior

Whether the content of a `ScrollFrame` stretches when dragged beyond its end and springs back. The stretch shows the player that the end was reached.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WhenScrollable` | 0 | Only on an axis where the canvas is longer than the frame. A list too short to scroll does not move. |
| `Always` | 1 | On every axis the frame scrolls along, even when the content fits. |
| `Never` | 2 | Never. Scrolling stops hard at each end. |

## Enum.FocusLossReason

Why a `TextInput` lost keyboard focus. `FocusLost` passes it along with `submitted`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Submitted` | 0 | The player pressed Return in a field that releases focus on submit. |
| `Moved` | 1 | The player pressed somewhere else, or pressed Tab to go to the next field. |
| `Canceled` | 2 | The player pressed Escape. With `RevertOnEscape` on, the text is restored to what it was when the field gained focus. |
| `Cancelled` | 2 | Deprecated: use `Canceled`. The old name still works. |
| `Script` | 3 | A script called `ReleaseFocus`, another field called `CaptureFocus`, or the field left the screen. |

## Enum.GradientTileMode

What a `UIGradient` draws beyond the ends of its sequence.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Clamp` | 0 | The colors at the two ends continue outward. |
| `Repeat` | 1 | The sequence repeats from its start. A seam shows where its two ends differ. |
| `Mirror` | 2 | The sequence repeats alternately backward and forward, so no seam shows. |

## Enum.GradientType

The shape of a `UIGradient`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | 0 | A straight gradient across the object, in the direction `Rotation` gives. `Offset` moves its center. |
| `Radial` | 1 | A gradient outward from the center of the object, plus `Offset`, to a radius of (width + height) / 4. `Rotation` has no effect. |
| `Conical` | 2 | A gradient that sweeps one full turn clockwise around the center of the object, plus `Offset`, starting in the direction `Rotation` gives. |

## Enum.GraphicsGroup

The groups of graphics settings that an options menu typically shows. A group is set to a level as a whole.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ViewDistance` | 0 | How far objects are drawn, and the detail of distant terrain. |
| `AntiAliasing` | 1 | How edges are smoothed. |

| `Shadows` | 3 | The resolution, cascades and distance of shadows, and contact shadows. |
| `GlobalIllumination` | 4 | Ambient occlusion and bounced light. |
| `Reflections` | 5 | What shiny surfaces reflect: reflection probes and screen-space reflections. |
| `Textures` | 6 | The size, filtering and streaming of textures. |
| `Effects` | 7 | Particles. |
| `Foliage` | 8 | The density of foliage. |
| `Shading` | 9 | The number of lights per frame, and shading detail. |

## Enum.GraphicsLevel

The level of one group of graphics settings.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Low` | 0 | The lowest level. |
| `Medium` | 1 | Between `Low` and `High`. |
| `High` | 2 | The default level. |
| `Ultra` | 3 | The highest level for play. |
| `Cinematic` | 4 | A level meant for recorded footage instead of play. It is currently the same as `Ultra`. |

## Enum.GraphicsQuality

An overall quality level of `GraphicsService`: one of four presets, or `Custom` or `Auto`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Low` | 0 | The lowest preset: three quarters of the resolution, short soft shadows, and no bloom or ambient occlusion. |
| `Medium` | 1 | The preset a handheld device starts with. |
| `High` | 2 | The preset a desktop starts with. |
| `Ultra` | 3 | The highest preset. |
| `Custom` | 4 | The value `QualityLevel` reads when any quality setting differs from its preset. It cannot be set. |
| `Auto` | 5 | The preset that was measured as suitable for this machine. |

## Enum.IKControlType

What an `IKControl` does to its joints.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TwoBone` | 0 | A limb of two bones, such as an arm or a leg, is bent so that its end reaches the target. |

## Enum.InputActionType

The kind of value an `InputAction` produces, which is what `GetState` returns. Every binding of an action produces this type, whatever device it reads.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Bool` | 0 | Pressed or not. `GetState` returns a boolean. Only this type fires `Pressed` and `Released`. |
| `Direction1D` | 1 | One signed axis. `GetState` returns a number: -1 to 1 from a pair of keys, or the analog value of a trigger or a wheel. |
| `Direction2D` | 2 | Two signed axes. `GetState` returns a `Vector2`, from a stick, from pointer movement or from the four direction keys of a binding. |
| `Direction3D` | 3 | Three signed axes. `GetState` returns a `vector`. No binding can drive three axes yet, so the value is always the zero vector. |
| `ViewportPosition` | 4 | The position of the pointer, not its movement. `GetState` returns a `Vector2` in window pixels, measured from the top left. |

## Enum.InputDeviceType

A kind of input device. `InputService.LastInputDeviceType` reports the kind the player used most recently, so that a HUD can switch its prompts. `InputBinding.DeviceType` reports the kind a binding belongs to, which `GetPreferredBinding` uses.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `KeyboardMouse` | 0 | A keyboard or a mouse. |
| `Gamepad` | 1 | A gamepad. |
| `Touch` | 2 | A touchscreen. A finger on the screen makes this the last device used, so a game can show on-screen controls only when they are needed. A binding to a virtual key code, such as `Enum.KeyCode.Virtual1`, also reports this type. |
| `XR` | 3 | A headset's controllers, or the hands it tracks. Its key codes are the ones whose names begin with `XR`. |

## Enum.InputRate

Whether the actions of an `InputContext` are dispatched on simulation ticks or on rendered frames. It is set per context and is independent of `Priority`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Simulation` | 0 | On simulation ticks, at the fixed tick rate. This is the default. It is deterministic and recorded in a replay; use it for everything that affects gameplay. |
| `Render` | 1 | On rendered frames, with a variable time step. Use it for camera look and UI, where a tick of delay is visible. Input read here depends on the frame rate and is not recorded in a replay, so do not base gameplay decisions on it. |

## Enum.IrradianceMode

What light an `IrradianceVolume` computes, and how it is combined with the ambient light.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Full` | 0 | All the indirect light a surface receives: the sky through every opening, and all bounced light. Inside the volume it replaces the sky's light and `Lighting.Ambient`. |
| `BounceOnly` | 1 | Bounced light only: light reflected from surfaces that the sun and other lights illuminate, and from emissive surfaces. It is added to the sky's light and `Lighting.Ambient`, which apply as they do outside the volume. Use it where the ambient light is set by hand or by the time of day and should stay as set. |

## Enum.ItemLineAlignment

Where a child of a `UIListLayout` is placed across its line.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Automatic` | 0 | On a `UIFlexItem`, the layout's setting is used. On the layout, the layout's own alignment across the line is used. |
| `Start` | 1 | At the start of the line's cross axis: the top of a row, or the left of a column. |
| `Center` | 2 | In the middle of the line. |
| `End` | 3 | At the end of the line's cross axis: the bottom of a row, or the right of a column. |
| `Stretch` | 4 | Stretched across the line: as tall as its row, or as wide as its column. |

| `Virtual1` | 97 | A virtual input, set by `InputService:SetVirtualState` instead of by hardware. It is bound, prioritized and recorded in a replay like any other key code. Use virtual inputs for on-screen buttons and thumbsticks.<br><br>A virtual input holds a number, not a press. A button sets 1 and 0, and a slider sets any value in between. The first four are also the axes of the two virtual sticks, `VirtualStick1` and `VirtualStick2`. |

## Enum.LineJoinMode

How a `UIStroke` draws a corner.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Round` | 0 | Rounded, as an arc the width of the stroke. |
| `Bevel` | 1 | Cut off flat across the corner. |
| `Miter` | 2 | Extended to a sharp point. |

## Enum.LipSyncMode

The method a `LipSync` uses to move a mouth.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Auto` | 0 | The best method available. It is the line's viseme track if the language being heard has one; otherwise the sound's frequency bands, if the face map has targets for them; otherwise the sound's loudness. |
| `Bands` | 1 | The sound's frequency bands, even if the line has a viseme track. They tell an open mouth from a wide or a round one. |
| `Loudness` | 2 | The sound's loudness only, which opens a single morph target. |

## Enum.LogLevel

The severity of a log message, in ascending order. `Value` orders the levels, so a handler can filter with `level.Value >= Enum.LogLevel.Warning.Value`. `DebugService.MessageOut` passes one with every message.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Trace` | 0 | Very detailed output, per frame or per call. It is not shown in a normal run. |
| `Debug` | 1 | Diagnostic detail for whoever is working on the code that logs it. |
| `Info` | 2 | Ordinary information. `print` logs at this level. |
| `Warning` | 3 | Something is wrong, and the run continues. `warn` logs at this level. |
| `Error` | 4 | A failure that the code could not handle, including an error raised in a signal handler. |

## Enum.NetworkState

The connection state of this machine, reported by `NetworkService.State`. `Join`, `Host` and `Disconnect` change it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Offline` | 0 | Single-player: no other machine is connected, and this machine is the authority. |
| `Connecting` | 1 | `Join` was called, and the server has not answered yet. |
| `Connected` | 2 | In a match on another machine's authority: this machine is a client. |
| `Hosting` | 3 | This machine is the authority, has a player of its own, and others can join. |
| `Serving` | 4 | A dedicated server, started with `--serve`: it is the authority and has no player. |
| `Reconnecting` | 5 | The connection to the server was lost, and this machine is trying to connect again. The world stays as it was; a game can show a message and stop predicting. |

## Enum.NetworkTopology

The network role of this process, reported by `NetworkService.Topology`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Solo` | 0 | Single-player: nothing is networked, and this process is the authority. |
| `Host` | 1 | The authority of a match, with a player of its own in the same process. |
| `Dedicated` | 2 | The authority of a match with no player of its own: a server with no window. |
| `Replica` | 3 | A client connected to another machine's authority. It shows the world it is sent. |

## Enum.OrientationAlignmentMode

The target an `AlignOrientation` turns toward.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OneAttachment` | 0 | The constraint's own `CFrame`. |
| `TwoAttachment` | 1 | The constraint's `Attachment1`. |

## Enum.PartShape

The built-in solid that a `Part` is drawn and collides as.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Block` | 0 | A box. |
| `Ball` | 1 | A sphere. |
| `Cylinder` | 2 | A cylinder that stands along the Y axis. |
| `Capsule` | 3 | A cylinder with a hemisphere at each end, along the Y axis. |
| `Wedge` | 4 | A ramp: a box cut diagonally, with one sloped face. |

## Enum.ParticleCollision

What the particles of a `ParticleEmitter` collide with.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | Nothing. Particles pass through the world. |
| `SceneDepth` | 1 | The surfaces that are drawn. On the GPU, the depth of the picture is used: every surface on screen, but nothing off screen or hidden behind another surface. On the CPU, a ray is cast against the parts in the particle's way. |
| `Terrain` | 2 | The terrain, whether it is in view or not. Most sparks, rain and debris land on it. |
| `Both` | 3 | The terrain and the surfaces that are drawn. |

## Enum.ParticleCollisionResponse

What a particle does when it hits something.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Bounce` | 0 | It bounces, keeping the share of its speed that `Bounce` sets and losing speed along the surface by `Friction`. It comes to rest when it barely rises. |
| `Stick` | 1 | It stays where it landed for the rest of its life. |
| `Kill` | 2 | It is removed, like rain on a roof or a spark on water. |

## Enum.ParticleFlipbookMode

How a particle plays the frames of its emitter's flipbook.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Loop` | 0 | The frames play in order at `FlipbookFramerate`, repeating. Use it for fire, a flag or a glint. |
| `OverLife` | 1 | The frames play once over the particle's life, and the last is held at the end. Use it for a puff of smoke or an explosion. |
| `Random` | 2 | Each particle shows one frame, chosen at random when it is emitted. Use it for debris, leaves or a mix of shapes from one image. |

## Enum.ParticleShape

The shape a particle is drawn as when its emitter has no texture.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Soft` | 0 | A round shape that fades out toward its edge. Use it for smoke, dust, steam or a glow. |
| `Disc` | 1 | A round dot with a sharp edge. Use it for sparks, bubbles or confetti. |
| `Square` | 2 | A square that faces the camera. Use it for pixels, debris or square confetti. |

## Enum.ParticleSimulation

Whether the particles of a `ParticleEmitter` are simulated on the CPU or on the GPU.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Cpu` | 0 | On the CPU: a few thousand particles per emitter, sorted from back to front together with all other particles. It works on every machine. |
| `Gpu` | 1 | On the GPU: tens of thousands of particles per emitter for a few draw calls, emitted, moved and collided in a compute shader. They are not sorted among themselves, which is not visible with additive particles. |

## Enum.Platform

The operating system the game is running on, reported by `RunService.Platform`. Use it for the few things that depend on the system, such as store rules or a file path shown to the player. To decide what to show on screen, check what the machine has instead, with `InputService.TouchAvailable` and `UIService.ViewportSize`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Windows` | 0 | Windows. |
| `Linux` | 1 | Linux. |
| `MacOS` | 2 | macOS. |
| `Android` | 3 | Android. |
| `IOS` | 4 | iOS. |

## Enum.PlaybackState

The state of a `Tween`. It distinguishes a tween that finished from one that was stopped early.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Begin` | 0 | Created and not yet played. |
| `Delayed` | 1 | Playing, but still within its `TweenInfo.DelayTime`, so it is not changing the property yet. |
| `Playing` | 2 | Playing and changing the property. |
| `Paused` | 3 | Paused at its current position. `Play` resumes from there. |
| `Completed` | 4 | Reached its end. The property has exactly its goal value. |
| `Canceled` | 5 | Stopped before its end by `Cancel`. The property keeps the value it had reached. |
| `Cancelled` | 5 | Deprecated: use `Canceled`. The old name still works. |

## Enum.PositionAlignmentMode

The target an `AlignPosition` pulls toward.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OneAttachment` | 0 | The constraint's own `Position`. |
| `TwoAttachment` | 1 | The constraint's `Attachment1`. |

## Enum.PromiseState

The state of a `Promise`. A promise settles once and does not change afterward.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Started` | 0 | Not settled yet: neither resolved nor rejected. |
| `Resolved` | 1 | Resolved, with the values that `Await` returns. |
| `Rejected` | 2 | Rejected, with the values that its rejection handlers receive. |
| `Canceled` | 3 | Canceled before it settled. Its executor was stopped and its handlers do not run. |
| `Cancelled` | 3 | Deprecated: use `Canceled`. The old name still works. |

## Enum.RaycastFilterType

Whether the filter list of a `RaycastParams` names what a query can hit or what it ignores.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Exclude` | 0 | The query hits everything except the listed instances and their descendants. |
| `Include` | 1 | The query hits only the listed instances and their descendants. |

## Enum.RelayState

The state of a hosted match with its relay, reported by `NetworkService.RelayState`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | No relay was requested, or this machine is not hosting. The match can be joined by address. |
| `Connecting` | 1 | The relay was asked to register the match and has not answered yet. |
| `Ready` | 2 | The relay has registered the match, and others can join with `JoinCode`. |
| `Unreachable` | 3 | The relay does not answer, or refused. The engine keeps trying, and the match can still be joined by address. |

## Enum.RenderPriority

Reference priorities for `RunService:BindToRenderStep`, which takes a number. Use an item's `Value` plus or minus an offset: `Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1` runs just after the camera.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `First` | 0 | Before everything else in the frame. |
| `Input` | 100 | Where the input that the frame reads becomes intents. |
| `Camera` | 200 | Where the camera is positioned. The built-in camera rig runs here. |
| `Character` | 300 | After the camera, for anything that follows where the camera looks. |
| `Last` | 2000 | After everything else, just before `PreRender` fires. |

## Enum.Retargeting

How an `AnimationPlayer` adapts a clip made for one skeleton to another.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Automatic` | 0 | When both skeletons are humanoid, joints are matched by their role, such as hips, spine, arms and legs, which is found from common joint naming schemes. A clip made for one character then works on another with different proportions and joint names: each joint rotates by the same amount from its own rest pose, the hips move in proportion to the length of the legs, and every bone keeps its own length.<br><br>Otherwise, and always for two files that share one skeleton, joints are matched by name. |
| `ByName` | 1 | Joints are matched by name only, and the clip's transforms are applied unchanged. Use it for clothing on the body it was made for, or for a creature with its own clips. A joint that one side does not have is skipped silently. |

## Enum.RotationOrder

The order in which `CFrame.fromEuler` applies its three angles and `CFrame:ToEuler` returns them. The rotations are intrinsic: each is about the axes produced by the previous one, read from left to right.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `XYZ` | 0 | X, then Y, then Z. |
| `XZY` | 1 | X, then Z, then Y. |
| `YXZ` | 2 | Y (yaw), then X (pitch), then Z (roll). This is the default when `order` is omitted. |
| `YZX` | 3 | Y, then Z, then X. |
| `ZXY` | 4 | Z, then X, then Y. |
| `ZYX` | 5 | Z, then Y, then X. |

## Enum.RunContext

Where a `Script` runs, set by `Script.RunContext`. Inside a script service, the service decides instead. A single-player or hosting machine is both the server and a client, and runs each script once whatever its context.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Client` | 0 | On every machine that has a player: a client, a single-player game and a host. Never on a dedicated server, whose build does not include client scripts. |
| `Server` | 1 | On the authority: a dedicated server, a single-player game and a host. Never on a client that joined, whose build does not include server scripts. |
| `Shared` | 2 | On every machine, once each: the server and every client. This is the default outside the script services. |

## Enum.RunOutcome

How a run of the game ended on this machine, as `RunService:GetLastRun().Outcome` reports it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | There was no previous run, or its record was cleared. |
| `Clean` | 1 | The run was asked to end and ended normally. |
| `Crashed` | 2 | The run ended in a fault or an uncaught exception. Its report holds the crash note. |
| `Unfinished` | 3 | The run ended without being asked to and without a fault of its own: the system, the player or a power loss ended it. On a phone, this is the usual end of a game left in the background. |

## Enum.ScaleType

How an `ImageLabel` fits its image into its rectangle.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stretch` | 0 | The whole image fills the whole rectangle. Its aspect ratio is not kept. |
| `Slice` | 1 | Nine-slice scaling. The four corners are drawn at their own size, the four edges stretch along one axis and the center stretches along both. `SliceCenter` sets where the image is divided. Use it so a panel or a button keeps its rounded corners at any size. |
| `Tile` | 2 | The image is repeated at its own size until the rectangle is full. |
| `Fit` | 3 | The whole image is shown as large as fits in the rectangle with its aspect ratio kept, centered. The background shows where the image does not reach. Use it for an icon. |
| `Crop` | 4 | The image covers the whole rectangle with its aspect ratio kept, and what extends beyond is cut off equally on both sides. Use it for a picture that fills a card. |

## Enum.SceneLoadStatus

The stage of a `SceneLoad`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Preparing` | 0 | The scene's file is being read and its meshes are being loaded. |
| `Ready` | 1 | The scene is prepared and waiting for `Activate`. |
| `Activating` | 2 | The switch has started: the old scene is closing. |
| `Done` | 3 | The scene is open. |
| `Failed` | 4 | The scene could not be prepared. `Error` gives the reason. |
| `Canceled` | 5 | The load was canceled, by `Cancel` or by another load. |
| `Cancelled` | 5 | Deprecated: use `Canceled`. The old name still works. |

## Enum.ScreenOrientation

The orientations in which a game can be held on a device that rotates, set by `UIService.ScreenOrientation`. The two landscape orientations are named for the side the top of the device is on.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `LandscapeLeft` | 0 | Landscape, with the top of the device on the left. The screen does not rotate when the device is turned over. |
| `LandscapeRight` | 1 | Landscape, with the top of the device on the right. The screen does not rotate when the device is turned over. |
| `LandscapeSensor` | 2 | Either landscape orientation, following the device as it is turned over. This is the default. |
| `Portrait` | 3 | Portrait, with the device upright. |
| `Sensor` | 4 | Any orientation, following the device and the player's rotation lock. |

## Enum.ScreenSplit

How the window is divided between the local players on one machine.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | One picture, through `Workspace.CurrentCamera`. |
| `Columns` | 1 | One view for each local player that has a camera, side by side. |
| `Rows` | 2 | One view for each local player that has a camera, stacked one above another. |
| `Grid` | 3 | Two views side by side, or three or four views in the quarters of the window. |
| `Dynamic` | 4 | One picture while two players are close together, and two views divided by a line when they move apart. |

## Enum.ScrollingDirection

The axes along which a `ScrollFrame` scrolls.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X` | 1 | Horizontally only, as for a carousel. |
| `Y` | 2 | Vertically only, as for a list. |
| `XY` | 3 | Both ways, as for a map or a canvas larger than its frame in both directions. |

## Enum.SequenceControl

What a playing `SequencePlayer` does with the local players' input.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Keep` | 0 | Nothing. The players keep control during the sequence. |
| `Suspend` | 1 | The players' movement and actions read as released until the sequence ends. |

## Enum.SettingSource

Where the value of a graphics setting comes from, as `GraphicsService:GetSource` reports it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `CommandLine` | 0 | A command-line flag the game was started with. A script or the player cannot override it. |
| `Player` | 1 | The player's saved choice. |
| `Script` | 2 | A value a script set in this session, which has not been saved. |
| `Project` | 3 | The game's `project.toml`. |
| `Preset` | 4 | The current quality level. |
| `Engine` | 5 | The engine's default; nothing else set the value. |

## Enum.ShadowQuality

The quality of the sun's shadows: their resolution and their number of cascades.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Off` | 0 | The sun casts no shadows. |
| `Low` | 1 | 512 texels and two cascades. |
| `Medium` | 2 | 1024 texels and three cascades. |
| `High` | 3 | 2048 texels and four cascades. |
| `Ultra` | 4 | 2048 texels and four cascades, over a longer distance. |

## Enum.Shape2D

The outline a `Part2D` is drawn with and collides as.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Box` | 0 | A rectangle of the part's `Size`. |
| `Circle` | 1 | A circle whose diameter is the smaller of the part's two sizes. |
| `Capsule` | 2 | A rectangle with rounded ends at the top and bottom. Use it for a character: its rounded base slides over the seams between tiles instead of catching on them. |

## Enum.SortOrder

The order in which a layout arranges its children.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Name` | 0 | By `Name`, compared character by character. The order does not depend on the order the children were created in. |
| `LayoutOrder` | 1 | By each child's `LayoutOrder`, and by tree order for equal values. This is the usual choice, because a list can be reordered without renaming anything. |

## Enum.SoundCategory

The kind of sound a `Sound` is. It selects which of the player's three volume settings applies, and music is lowered while a voice plays.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Effects` | 0 | Everything that is not music or voice: a footstep, a door, a shot, the wind. |
| `Music` | 1 | Music. It is lowered while a `Voice` sound is audible (see `AudioService.MusicUnderVoice`). |
| `Voice` | 2 | Speech: a line of dialogue, a narrator or a spoken shout. |

## Enum.StartCorner

The corner from which a `UIGridLayout` starts filling.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TopLeft` | 0 | From left to right, then from top to bottom. |
| `TopRight` | 1 | From right to left, then from top to bottom. |
| `BottomLeft` | 2 | From left to right, then from bottom to top. |
| `BottomRight` | 3 | From right to left, then from bottom to top. |

## Enum.StreamingMode

How a `Model` is loaded and unloaded by world streaming.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Nonatomic` | 0 | Each descendant is streamed separately, by its own position. This is the default and suits loose scenery. |
| `Atomic` | 1 | The model is streamed as one unit: it belongs to a single cell however far its parts spread, and it loads and unloads whole. Use it for a building, or for a machine made of moving parts. |
| `Persistent` | 2 | The model is never streamed. It exists before the first tick and is never unloaded. Use it for a spawn point, a checkpoint or anything a script keeps a reference to. |

## Enum.StrokeSizingMode

The unit of a `UIStroke`'s `Thickness`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `FixedSize` | 0 | Pixels. |
| `ScaledSize` | 1 | A fraction of the parent's shorter side, or of the font size on text, so that the stroke grows with what it outlines. |

## Enum.SubtitleMode

When captions are shown, set by `DialogueService.Subtitles`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Auto` | 0 | Shown when the player does not hear the line in the language they read. That is the case when the voice language differs from the text language, the line fell back to the default language's recording, or the line has no recording. |
| `On` | 1 | Always shown. |
| `Off` | 2 | Never shown. |

Why a machine no longer has an agent of a `Swarm`, as `AgentRemoved` reports it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Removed` | 0 | The authority removed the agent. |
| `OutOfReach` | 1 | On a client: the agent left the client's replication radius. It still exists on the authority and is added again if it returns. |

| `Down` | 1 | Toward the bottom of the window. |
| `Left` | 2 | Toward the left of the window. |
| `Right` | 3 | Toward the right of the window. |

## Enum.TerrainPaintMode

What a stroke of `Terrain:PaintBall` does with the two materials a voxel holds, one over the other.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Replace` | 0 | The ground becomes the material, replacing what was there. |
| `Blend` | 1 | More of the material shows over what is there, by the strength of the stroke. |
| `Under` | 2 | The material is put under the material painted over it. |
| `Erase` | 3 | Less of the upper material shows, revealing the one under it. |

## Enum.TextInputKeyboard

The on-screen keyboard a phone shows for a `TextInput`. A desktop input method also reads it as a hint. A masked field always shows the password keyboard.

| `Number` | 1 | Digits. |
| `Decimal` | 2 | Digits and a decimal point. |
| `Phone` | 3 | A telephone keypad. |
| `Email` | 4 | Letters with `@` within easy reach, for an email address. |
| `Url` | 5 | Letters with `/` and `.` within easy reach, for a web address. |

## Enum.TextOverflow

What a `TextLabel` does with text that does not fit in it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Overflow` | 0 | The text is drawn beyond the edges of the label. |
| `Clip` | 1 | The text is cut at the edges of the label, even through the middle of a letter. |
| `Ellipsis` | 2 | The text is shortened at a whole character and ended with an ellipsis, so that it fits. |

## Enum.TextureFilter

How an image is sampled when it is drawn larger or smaller than its own size.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | 0 | Blended between neighboring pixels of the image. The result is smooth; use it for painted art. |
| `Nearest` | 1 | The nearest pixel of the image, with no blending. Pixels stay sharp at any zoom; use it for pixel art. |

## Enum.TextureMode

How the texture of a `Beam` or a `Trail` is laid along it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Stretch` | 0 | Once over the whole length, whatever the length. |
| `Wrap` | 1 | Repeated every `TextureLength` meters, measured from the start. On a trail, the texture slides along as the trail moves. |
| `Static` | 2 | Repeated every `TextureLength` meters and fixed where it was laid. On a trail, the texture stays over the ground it was drawn over, like a tire mark. On a beam, the texture does not scroll. |

## Enum.TextureQuality

How much of each texture is loaded into memory.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Low` | 0 | A quarter of each side. |
| `Medium` | 1 | Half of each side. |
| `High` | 2 | The full size. |

## Enum.UIDragDetectorDragStyle

How a `UIDragDetector` turns the pointer's movement into its object's movement.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TranslatePlane` | 0 | The object follows the pointer on both axes. |
| `TranslateLine` | 1 | The object moves only along `DragAxis`, like the thumb of a slider. |
| `Rotate` | 2 | The object rotates about its center as the pointer moves around it, like a dial. |
| `Scriptable` | 3 | The object does not move. The detector's events report the pointer's position, and a script decides what to do. |

## Enum.UIDragDetectorResponseStyle

What a `UIDragDetector` changes when its object is dragged.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Offset` | 0 | The offset of the object's `Position`. |
| `Scale` | 1 | The scale of the object's `Position`, as a fraction of its parent. |
| `CustomOffset` | 2 | Nothing. `DragUDim2` and `DragRotation` report the drag as an offset, and a script applies it. |
| `CustomScale` | 3 | Nothing. `DragUDim2` reports the drag as a fraction of the parent, and a script applies it. |

## Enum.UIFlexAlignment

What a `UIListLayout` does with the space its children leave over along one axis.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | Nothing. The children stay where the alignment puts them. |
| `Fill` | 1 | The children grow by equal amounts until the space is used. |
| `SpaceAround` | 2 | The space is placed around each child: a full share between two children and half a share at each end. |
| `SpaceBetween` | 3 | The space is placed between the children, with none at the ends. |
| `SpaceEvenly` | 4 | The space is placed in equal shares between the children and at both ends. |

## Enum.UIFlexMode

How one child of a `UIListLayout` takes up leftover space or gives up space when there is too little.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | The child keeps its size. |
| `Grow` | 1 | The child grows into leftover space and never shrinks. |
| `Shrink` | 2 | The child shrinks when the line is too long and never grows. |
| `Fill` | 3 | The child both grows and shrinks. |
| `Custom` | 4 | The child grows by its `GrowRatio` and shrinks by its `ShrinkRatio`. |

## Enum.UpscalingMode

The method used to scale the world up to the window's resolution when `GraphicsService.RenderScale` is below 1.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | Plain filtering, as when an image is stretched. |
| `FSR1` | 1 | AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1: an upscale that preserves edges, followed by sharpening. |
| `FSR2` | 2 | AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2: a temporal upscale that builds each pixel of the window from several frames, each drawn with a subpixel offset. It also does the anti-aliasing: `AntiAliasing` is ignored on frames it upscales, and at a `RenderScale` of 1 it acts as anti-aliasing only.<br><br>AMD's names for the scales are quality (0.67), balanced (0.59), performance (0.5) and ultra performance (0.33). It applies to the main view of a perspective camera, on a device with compute shaders; everything else is upscaled with FSR 1. |

## Enum.UserInputType

The kind of input an `InputObject` comes from, in the input events of `InputService`. It is coarser than `KeyCode`: read it when the handler only needs the kind of input, and read `KeyCode` for the specific key.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `None` | 0 | No input. It is the value of an `InputObject` that no event produced. |
| `Keyboard` | 1 | A keyboard key. `KeyCode` gives the key. |
| `MouseButton1` | 2 | The primary mouse button, normally the left one. |
| `MouseButton2` | 3 | The secondary mouse button, normally the right one. |
| `MouseButton3` | 4 | The middle mouse button, usually the wheel pressed in. |
| `MouseMovement` | 5 | The pointer moved. It fires `InputChanged` only, never `InputBegan` or `InputEnded`. |
| `MouseWheel` | 6 | The mouse wheel turned. It fires `InputChanged`, with the amount in `Delta.z`; one notch is 1. |
| `Gamepad` | 7 | A gamepad button or stick. `KeyCode` gives which. A stick's movement fires `InputChanged`, with the axis value in `Position`. |
| `Touch` | 8 | A finger on a touchscreen. It fires `InputBegan` when the finger touches, `InputChanged` as it moves and `InputEnded` when it lifts, with `Position` in window pixels and `TouchId` identifying the finger. Even a very short tap begins and ends.<br><br>These events fire whether or not the interface used the touch. Use them for a game's own on-screen controls, which drive actions through `InputService:SetVirtualState`. |
| `XRLeft` | 9 | The left controller of a headset, or the left hand it tracks. `KeyCode` gives which button, trigger or stick. `HapticService` vibrates this controller under this type. |
| `XRRight` | 10 | The right controller of a headset, or the right hand it tracks. See `XRLeft`. |

## Enum.VehicleTransmission

How a `VehicleController`'s gearbox chooses its gear.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Automatic` | 0 | It shifts by itself, by the engine's turns a minute. |
| `Manual` | 1 | It stays in the gear the controller's `Gear` asks for. |

## Enum.VelocityConstraintMode

How much of the velocity a `LinearVelocity` controls.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Line` | 0 | Only the speed along a line. |
| `Plane` | 1 | Only the velocity within a plane. |
| `Vector` | 2 | The whole velocity. |

## Enum.VerticalAlignment

An alignment along the Y axis. `TextLabel.TextYAlignment` aligns text with it, and a layout's `VerticalAlignment` aligns children with it.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Top` | 0 | Aligned to the top edge. |
| `Center` | 1 | Centered vertically. |
| `Bottom` | 2 | Aligned to the bottom edge. |

## Enum.VibrationMotor

One of the vibration motors of a controller, for `HapticService`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Large` | 0 | The heavy, slow motor, which gives a rumble. |
| `Small` | 1 | The light, fast motor, which gives a buzz. |
| `LeftTrigger` | 2 | The motor in the left trigger, on a controller that has one. |
| `RightTrigger` | 3 | The motor in the right trigger, on a controller that has one. |
| `LeftHand` | 4 | The left of two controllers held one in each hand. No supported device has one yet, so it always reports as unsupported. |
| `RightHand` | 5 | The right of two controllers held one in each hand. No supported device has one yet, so it always reports as unsupported. |

## Enum.ViewQuality

How completely a `CameraTexture` or a `SubWorld` view is drawn.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Full` | 0 | Everything the main view draws, including shadows and post-processing effects. |
| `Simple` | 1 | No shadows and no post-processing effects. It suits a monitor feed or a minimap. |

## Enum.WaterShape

The extent of a `Water`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Ocean` | 0 | Everywhere, with no edge. |
| `Box` | 1 | A rectangle. It is the earlier name of `Pool` and behaves the same. |
| `Spline` | 2 | A level river in straight segments from one `WaterPoint` child to the next. Every point is at the water's `SurfaceLevel`, whatever its own height. For a river that curves and descends, use `River`. |
| `Lake` | 3 | The area inside the closed curve through its `WaterPoint` children, level at `SurfaceLevel`. It needs at least three points. |
| `River` | 4 | A ribbon along the curve through its `WaterPoint` children, from the first to the last. The height of each point is the height of the surface there, so a river can descend. Each point's `Width` and `Depth` set the river's width and depth there. |
| `Pool` | 5 | A rectangle of `Size`, centered on `Position`. |

## Enum.WindowMode

How the game's window uses the display.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Windowed` | 0 | A window with a border. |
| `Borderless` | 1 | A window with no border that covers the whole display. Switching to other windows stays fast. |
| `Fullscreen` | 2 | Exclusive use of the whole display. |

## Enum.XRHand

A hand, or the controller it holds, for `XRService`.

| Item | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Left` | 0 | The left hand. |
| `Right` | 1 | The right hand. |
